written: before running GitTrace or Bandit on this target (held-out: chosen and read only after the rule fixes were final)
sources: README.md 'Scenarios': Code Execution (OS Command Injection #1, #2), Injection (SQL Injection, XSS, log/HTML injection), Authorization Bypass (JWT Token Forge, ...), Miscellaneous (weak password protection, path traversal)
reading of app.py, config.py, setup.py, core/*.py at the pinned commit
notes: Both documented OS command injections run through the one dangerous call, helpers.run_cmd -> os.popen(cmd): #1 importPaste builds 'curl --insecure {url}' from its arguments (views.py:210-211), #2 systemDiagnostics passes cmd (views.py:345, after an admin-password check in the handler body) and systemDebug passes 'ps {}'.format(arg) (views.py:352). Listed once, at the sink.

Every resolver is reached through POST /graphql, registered with app.add_url_rule(view_func=OverriddenView.as_view(...)) and dispatched by graphene; GitTrace detects neither form, so no tool is expected to show this reachability statically.
Out of GitTrace's categories and not listed: XSS, log/HTML injection, JWT decoded without verifying the signature, path traversal in uploadPaste, SSRF in importPaste.
app.py:28 os.popen('python3 setup.py') is a constant command; app.py:10 app.secret_key = os.urandom(24) is random.

vulnerabilities.detail: os.popen(cmd) with cmd built from GraphQL arguments by its callers
User(..., password="password123"): the seeded operator account's password, passed as a keyword argument
